name: alloc-small
algorithm: A ring of 4,096 live heap objects of 8 to 256 bytes (sizes and contents from splitmix64), each step reading the oldest, allocating and filling a new one, then freeing the old, through each language's std general-purpose allocator; the wrapping sum of each object's length, first and last byte (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; allocation has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares allocators; every column makes the same objects in the same order, and the checksum reads every object once
notes: Allocators named (B20's rule, applied to allocators): mk std's general heap (sys.heap.Alloc(), HeapList[u8] objects); c malloc and free of the static UCRT; rust System (HeapAlloc); zig std.heap.smp_allocator; go the garbage-collected runtime allocator (GOGC=100, labelled: it frees in batches); cs the Workstation GC heap (byte[] via Span.ToArray, labelled: frees in batches).
